title: Horizontal Drain Fittings: Why Sanitary Tees Fail
description: Using a standard sanitary tee in a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage application is one of the most common installation mistakes in residential plumbing. A sanitary tee has a short sweep designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. When installed horizontally, the short curve fails to direct solid waste smoothly along the pipe axis, causing waste to splash, build up, and eventually form severe clogs. Correct code compliance and long-term reliability require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-turn TY fitting for horizontal directional changes, ensuring proper hydraulic flow and preventing premature system blockages.

Horizontal Drain Fittings: Why Sanitary Tees Fail

Using a standard sanitary tee in a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage application is one of the most common installation mistakes in residential plumbing. A sanitary tee has a short sweep designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. When installed horizontally, the short curve fails to direct solid waste smoothly along the pipe axis, causing waste to splash, build up, and eventually form severe clogs. Correct code compliance and long-term reliability require a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-turn TY fitting for horizontal directional changes, ensuring proper hydraulic flow and preventing premature system blockages.
